html:
SMTO-CAP-0005 — SMTO couldn't confirm a safe way or place to do this step

GUID: e965fd28-f447-4e55-912f-20514703a22a
Slug: capability-adapter-unavailable
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • SMTO stopped this step because it couldn't confirm the tool it needed, or the USB or external drive it should save to. Nothing was written or run by this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you asked SMTO to save to a USB or external drive, make sure it's plugged into the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer). SMTO asks the Gateway for the list of connected drives, and a drive that isn't mounted can't be confirmed.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for the Gateway this Task uses. If SMTO can't reach the Gateway, it can't list the drives or use tools on that computer.
  3. Reply in the Task with the drive's full folder path, exactly as that computer's file manager shows it, and ask SMTO to continue. An exact path lets SMTO check the destination instead of guessing between drives.
  4. If no drive was involved, open Capabilities by the message box and check that the tool or Skill you need isn't set to Never or − Exclude. SMTO only uses tools allowed for this Task and won't swap in a different one.

What success looks like

  • SMTO confirms the destination or tool, the step runs, and the files appear where you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and the Gateway. Don't turn off Protect removable destinations to get past this; that check is what stops SMTO from writing to the wrong drive.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The operation was refused before execution because no concrete adapter is in the run's capability scope, or the removable-destination guard could not obtain a complete drive inventory or a valid path binding from the selected Gateway.

What this means

  • Discovery has no concrete adapter in scope, or removable-destination validation cannot establish usable inventory/path evidence. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • Discovery has no concrete adapter in scope, or removable-destination validation cannot establish usable inventory/path evidence.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish missing adapter discovery from unavailable removable-destination evidence using the retained source/stage and target inventory.

How to fix it

  • For removable writes, check that the Gateway's removable_destinations file operation returns ok and complete with at most 32 rows, and that the destination path is under 4096 characters with no control characters (guard, _observe and _path_binding in src/agent_runtime/native/removable_destinations.py). For discovery, confirm the tool is in ToolCatalog.capabilities for this run (not excluded, Ask mode or upstream-limited) and select an exact available tool.
  • Restore the relevant adapter or destination inventory, then select the exact intended target without broadening authority.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected operation has a concrete allowed adapter and any required destination evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
